USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Why conjugation matters

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A medical student studies the vaccine that prevents most classic Hib epiglottitis. It links a capsular polysaccharide to a carrier protein. What immunologic advantage is especially important for protecting infants and young children?

  1. Recruitment of T-cell help and immunologic memory
  2. T-cell-independent activation with predominantly short-lived IgM
  3. Passive transfer of preformed antibodies from the vaccine
  4. Selective induction of cytotoxic T cells without antibody production
  5. Suppression of germinal-center formation to limit inflammation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Recruitment of T-cell help and immunologic memory

Protein conjugation permits T-cell-dependent responses to the polysaccharide antigen, improving infant responses and memory.

Understanding the options

Recruitment of T-cell help and immunologic memory
Protein conjugation permits T-cell-dependent responses to the polysaccharide antigen, improving infant responses and memory.
T-cell-independent activation with predominantly short-lived IgM
Protein conjugation is intended to overcome the limited infant response to unconjugated polysaccharides.
Passive transfer of preformed antibodies from the vaccine
Conjugate vaccines generate active immunity rather than supplying preformed protective immunoglobulin.
Selective induction of cytotoxic T cells without antibody production
Protection against the capsule depends importantly on antibody responses supported by T-cell help.
Suppression of germinal-center formation to limit inflammation
Conjugation supports the immune processes that produce effective antibody and memory rather than suppressing them.
